title: Scroll snap
learningObjectives: Explain scroll snap and use visual effects responsibly.

understand.concept: CSS Scroll Snap lets a scroll container define snap positions for its children. scroll-snap-type controls the axis and strictness; scroll-snap-align sets the alignment point on each snap item; scroll-padding and scroll-margin adjust snap positions.
understand.whyItMatters: Scroll snapping can improve carousels and section navigation, but it should not trap users or prevent free scrolling. Test touch, keyboard, reduced motion, and content of different heights.
understand.analogy: Scroll snap is like a guide that helps a scrolling page settle at meaningful positions without removing the ability to scroll.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS compositing and animation timelines follow browser rendering rules.

explain.narrative: Each card snaps to the start edge as the user scrolls horizontally. The container remains scrollable.

examples.explanation: Each card snaps to the start edge as the user scrolls horizontally. The container remains scrollable.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the visual effect or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Build a horizontal card strip with scroll snap. Ensure users can scroll freely and that keyboard focus can reach every card.
practise.independentTask: Build a visual component using the effect. Include a fallback, check contrast, and test keyboard and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Keep essential content independent of visual effects.
Check browser support and fallback behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which property sets the snap behaviour and axis on a scroll container?
questions.explanation: scroll-snap-type defines the scroll axis and snap strictness.

questions.prompt: What should accompany an advanced visual effect?
options: A readable fallback and accessible content
Essential meaning available only through the effect
An assumption that all browsers support it
questions.answer: A readable fallback and accessible content
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement keeps the interface usable when effects are unsupported or disabled.
